subject: English
caption:
Active voice, spotted in three seconds: add 'by zombies'.

If you can put 'by zombies' after the verb and the sentence still works, it's passive.

'The window was broken by zombies.' Works — passive.
'The boy broke the window by zombies.' Nonsense — active.

It sounds like a joke. It is also the fastest reliable test anyone has found, and it survives into A-level.

Bookmark it — you'll want it in December.

subject: French
caption:
Why your child can pass French and still not speak it.

Why a child can score well in French and still freeze in Paris.

Written exams reward recall. Speaking requires retrieval under time pressure, which is a different skill using a different part of the memory, and almost nothing in a school term practises it.

A vocabulary list learned on Sunday and tested on Friday is stored, not owned.

Ask when your child last had to answer a question in French without knowing it was coming.

caption:
If money is the reason you're hesitating, say so.

It's the most common reason and the least often said out loud, and it usually leads to a worse decision made quietly — a cheaper option that doesn't work, or nothing at all.

Tell us the number that's realistic. Sometimes the answer is fewer sessions targeted at one gap rather than a weekly commitment, and that genuinely works.
